about: How a bounded program's stderr is read as its memory limit. Go 1.27 can stop a program at its limit with SIGSEGV in the collector's span queue (golang/go#82667); only that fault, never another segmentation fault, is the limit.

mutants.name: gcoom-fault-unread
mutants.rule: A span-queue SIGSEGV at address 0 under a limit is the limit, not an unexplained crash.

mutants.name: gcoom-any-frame
mutants.rule: A fatal SIGSEGV in any frame but the span queue stays a crash.

mutants.name: gcoom-any-address
mutants.rule: A span-queue SIGSEGV at an address other than 0 is not the nil ring and stays a crash.

mutants.name: gcoom-watcher-drops-fault
mutants.rule: What a Watcher hands to Check keeps the span-queue fault.

mutants.name: gcoom-issue-unnamed
mutants.rule: The limit error of a span-queue fault names the Go runtime bug, so a reader does not take it for a clean out-of-memory report.
